solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Politeness makes Rosy cute

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made into something new, so the verb here signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Good manners turn someone sweet and charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is the only anagram signal: ROSYCUTE rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: civility and good manners are both politeness.

clue.text: Network company books in which you and I will have entry

indicators.note: the pair of letters admits another pair, which enters between them

parts.note: B is book, so BB is books
together you and I are we

explanation.surface: A network firm's books with a shared entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web is a fine network of threads.

clue.text: Left alone, apparently

parts.note: something left alone has had nothing done to it, so it stays unchanged

explanation.surface: Seemingly abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left alone' suggests abandoned or lonely; read it as untouched, with nobody having changed anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nobody has interfered with stays as it was, unchanged and unmodified.

clue.text: Shoplifter's dilemma?

parts.note: a thief in a shop must decide whether to pocket the goods or not; the phrase is also a final offer

explanation.surface: The choice a would-be thief faces in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday phrase means a non-negotiable offer; here it is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief's choice between stealing goods or not, phrased as the idiom for a final offer.

clue.text: April's wild winds heading south

indicators.note: the letter for south goes at the head, in front of the rest

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run in a disordered order

explanation.surface: Gusty April gales blowing southwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' reads as gales, but it is a verb, twists; 'heading south' is not a direction but S at the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To coil or twist round and round, as a road winds up a hill.

clue.text: Transposing the bookmakers' sign language is part of the strategy

indicators.note: transposing swaps the two halves of the word, sending the front syllable to the back

parts.note: tic-tac is the hand-signalling used by racecourse bookies

explanation.surface: Bookies' hand signals form part of a betting plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Tic-tac is the arm-waving code British racecourse bookmakers use to pass on odds; 'Transposing' swaps its halves, TIC and TAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A single manoeuvre or move is one component of an overall plan of campaign.

clue.text: Ignore letters — leave the office

definitions.meaning: neglect the mail by giving up on it
desert a job or duty station

explanation.surface: Skip the correspondence and walk out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is both mail and a position; giving up either fits the idiom for deserting duty.

clue.text: Hearing difficulty

definitions.meaning: a court case heard before a judge

explanation.surface: A problem with one's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing difficulty' suggests deafness; split it into a court case and a hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: A court case is heard before a judge, and a tribulation is a trying ordeal.

clue.text: Wild Etruscan horsemen

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Untamed riders from ancient Etruria.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythical creatures half man and half horse are literally horse-men.

clue.text: Bids for chests without a top

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is taken off

parts.note: coffers are strongboxes for valuables

explanation.surface: Offers made for lidless trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: bids at an auction are proposals of a price.

clue.text: Possibly fired — making space needing to be filled

definitions.meaning: a cartridge with no bullet that may be shot off
a gap on a form left empty

explanation.surface: Someone sacked, leaving a vacancy to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy round can be shot from a gun, and an empty gap on a form bears the same name.

clue.text: Result of a blow to the economy?

definitions.text: Result of a blow to the economy?

parts.words: Result of a blow to the economy?
parts.note: blowing air into a balloon puffs it up; in economics rising prices are the swelling

explanation.surface: What follows when the economy takes a knock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' reads as a setback, but it is the breath that puffs something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, swelling from blowing air in; economically, a general rise in prices.

clue.text: Free extract — ie that will be broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters before it are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A free sample, to be aired on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like an adjective for the extract, but it is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To release or disentangle someone from a tight spot is a synonym of setting free.

clue.text: A current issue on the coast

definitions.text: A current issue on the coast

parts.words: A current issue on the coast
parts.note: a river's flow (a current) issues, or flows out, into the sea through this landform

explanation.surface: A topical matter concerning seaside towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current issue' suggests news, but it means the outflow of a river's current at its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan of silt where a river splits into channels before reaching the sea.

clue.text: New wars or old weapons

indicators.note: making something new remakes it, so these letters are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: Fresh conflicts fought with antique arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Shafts shot from bows were the missiles of earlier warfare.

clue.text: US politician who could resort to treason

indicators.note: re-sorting puts the letters into a different order

explanation.surface: An American lawmaker capable of betraying the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as 'turn to', but it is re-sort, rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the upper house of Congress is an example of a US politician.

clue.text: Takes a meal among sailors, though it causes delay

indicators.note: being among the sailors puts the eating inside their letters

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Eating with the crew holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness or slowness is what makes things run behind schedule.

clue.text: A loud and voluble description of a very rich society

definitions.text: description of a very rich society

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
voluble means talking readily and smoothly

explanation.surface: A noisy, talkative account of high society.
explanation.walkthrough: J K Galbraith's book 'The Affluent Society' is the phrase behind the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy and prosperous, as in the well-known phrase for a rich consumer society.

clue.text: Musician involved in a racket?

definitions.meaning: a swindler or cheat working a scam

explanation.surface: A player caught up in a noisy din or a criminal scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist is one sense; the other is someone who cheats or swindles.

clue.text: Broadcasts about races

definitions.meaning: team races where runners hand over a baton

explanation.surface: Coverage of sporting events.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing a signal onward, and team contests handing a baton runner to runner.

clue.text: Various indications it's not raining

definitions.meaning: sunshine and parched ground are signs of fine weather

explanation.surface: Assorted signs that the weather is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two and it reads as two weather signs: sunshine and dry ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: miscellaneous or assorted items are various ones.

clue.text: No fixed date for the Romans

definitions.text: No fixed date for the Romans

parts.words: No fixed date for the Romans
parts.note: the Latin phrase means 'without a day', used when proceedings are adjourned indefinitely

explanation.surface: Ancient Romans with no set appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin legal phrase for adjournment indefinitely, without a day appointed to resume.

clue.text: Bans untidy beards

indicators.note: untidy means messed about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A prohibition on scruffy facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude or prohibit someone formally is a synonym of banning.

clue.text: The land transformed by Ali

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country changed by a man named Ali.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African country is an example of a land.

clue.text: Princess to show hesitancy in speech after press is seen

indicators.note: the hesitation sound comes after the urging

parts.note: to press someone is to beg or urge them
um is the noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A royal faltering when the reporters appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' suggests journalists, but it is the verb urge. A begum is a Muslim noblewoman of the Indian subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for a high-ranking Muslim woman in South Asia, roughly a princess.

clue.text: The opposite of a water chute?

definitions.text: The opposite of a water chute?

parts.words: The opposite of a water chute?
parts.note: a water chute is a slide into water; swap water for earth and you get earth sliding down

explanation.surface: Asking what is the reverse of a fairground water slide.
explanation.walkthrough: A water chute sends people sliding down into water; the opposite sends earth sliding.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse of earth down a slope, also an overwhelming election victory.

clue.text: Like a high-flier, able to take the long view?

definitions.text: Like a high-flier, able to take the long view?

parts.words: Like a high-flier, able to take the long view?
parts.note: a soaring bird of prey spots small things from a great height

explanation.surface: An ambitious high achiever with long-term vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests a career star, but it is a soaring raptor with sharp sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Having very keen sight, like a bird of prey that spots quarry from afar.

clue.text: Love for a particular kind of musical entertainment

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
per is Latin-derived for 'for each', as in so much per head

explanation.surface: Adoration of one specific musical genre.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged drama sung to orchestral accompaniment is one specific form of musical show.

clue.text: Appeals for casual worker, a good man, to return

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: returning means coming back the other way, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: ST, short for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A plea for a temp and a decent fellow to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeals' looks like a noun, requests, but it is the verb: attracts.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or entice someone is to attract them, as something appealing does.

clue.text: They look down in the mouth when at work

definitions.text: They look down in the mouth when at work

parts.words: They look down in the mouth when at work
parts.note: 'down in the mouth' means glum, but literally they peer down into patients' mouths

explanation.surface: People who seem miserable on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down in the mouth' is an idiom for gloomy, read literally here.
explanation.definitionFit: Practitioners who examine teeth peer into the open mouths of patients.
